Presentation follows the deploy-safe form; the hidden block informed only the rubric (demo/rubrics/osce-d4.json). Clinically shaped, not clinically reviewed. The finale's rehearsal at resident scale: a 72-year-old diabetic with a fever of 39.5, a pressure of 80, a lactate of 5.6 and a kidney full of pus behind a stone. The sepsis six inside the golden hour — cultures before the antibiotics, volume before the noradrenaline, and then the part protocols forget: the source. A dammed kidney reseeds the blood until urology opens a door for the pus.

effects.beat: — the niece: "Fever and shaking since yesterday, hardly any water passed. Her kidney stones ached all last week." A story with an address on it.
mottled knees, arms cold to the elbow, refill four seconds — the periphery closed its doors an hour ago
she flinches through the drowsiness at the right loin — cva tenderness, the pus signing its address
lactate 5.6 — the tissues running on debt; a number to clear, not just to file
two sets off different arms, urine bottled behind them — the lab gets its evidence before the bombardment
urine like weak tea, packed with white cells and bacteria — the source named on a strip
two grey cannulas, one in each fold — the bore is the resuscitation

then.beat: meropenem dosed to the kidneys, running in the first bag — the golden hour spent on what kills the killer

else.harm: the antibiotics flew before a single culture — the enemy will never be named

then.beat: thirty mils a kilo of warmed crystalloid through both barrels — the pressure lifts its head

else.beat: a litre crawling through one thin green line — bore first, then volume

then.beat: noradrenaline climbing by the minute — the map holds at 65 and stays there

else.beat: pressors into an empty tank — fill her first: vasoconstriction has nothing to squeeze

effects.beat: a catheter for the hourly truth — fifteen mils the first hour, a kidney whispering
ct shows a stone corking the right ureter — urology books the theatre tonight: the pus gets a door
the unit accepts her, pump and all
septic shock from an obstructed, infected kidney — named with its source and its clock

do.harm: half the resuscitation is speed — five minutes of shock on dry lines
the golden hour closed with no antimicrobial on board — every hour of delay stacks the odds against her
the tank is full and the pressure still sags — vasoplegia does not answer to volume
a dammed kidney reseeds the blood — the pressure sags against a rising pump

outcomes.label: Six boxes, one golden hour, and a door for the pus — the unit takes her warm
The hour was spent watching — multi-organ failure collected on schedule
